speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough for about six weeks now, and the breathlessness has been getting worse lately, especially when I try to walk up stairs. speaker: Doctor
text: That duration of six weeks suggests a subacute process; do you have any wheezing, chest tightness, or a history of smoking? REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray to check for infiltrates or masses.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest X-ray: Increased interstitial markings bilaterally, consistent with pulmonary fibrosis. No acute infiltrates or nodules.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF). Given the six-week history of progressive dyspnea, nocturnal cough, and the chest X-ray showing bilateral interstitial markings without acute infection, this clinical picture is most consistent with IPF. I recommend a High-Resolution CT (HRCT) scan to confirm the diagnosis and assess the extent of fibrosis.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with possible pulmonary fibrosis
